explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/99: 'Let A ⊆ ℝ² be a set of n points with minimum distance equal to 1, chosen to minimise the diameter of A. If n is sufficiently large then must there be three points in A which form an equilateral triangle of size 1?' The Lean statement: for all sufficiently large n, every n-point A ⊂ ℝ² with minimum distance exactly 1 (`HasMinDist1`: all distinct pairs at distance ≥ 1 and some pair at distance 1) that minimises the diameter among all such n-point sets (`IsMinOn` over {B | |B| = n ∧ HasMinDist1 B}) contains p, q, r with all three mutual distances equal to 1. This quantifies over every minimiser, which is the natural reading, and the 'sufficiently large n' is an `∀ᶠ n in atTop` as required (the site notes failure at n = 4). Faithful.
